summary.title: 我负责星载量子密钥分发接收机前端防护窗口的研发。接收机需要尽可能完整地接收
summary.question: 我负责星载量子密钥分发接收机前端防护窗口的研发。接收机需要尽可能完整地接收 1530–1565 nm 电信波段的单光子信号，同时尽可能反射 400–700 nm 波段的可见光太阳背景，以降低空间太阳散射和探测器杂散光对量子信号接收的影响。请在空气入射、熔融石英基底的条件下，仅使用 HfO2 和 SiO2 设计一个平面多层介质膜，膜系总层数不超过 30 层。

problem.compatibility_reason: Planar isotropic dielectric multilayer design within transfer-matrix method scope.
assumptions: Materials behave as linear isotropic dielectrics

metrics.rationale: 用户明确要求'尽可能完整地接收 1530–1565 nm 电信波段的单光子信号'，需要最大化该波段的平均透射率以确保量子信号接收完整性
用户要求'尽可能反射 400–700 nm 波段的可见光太阳背景'以降低杂散光影响，这是明确的阻带反射要求，使用 reflectance_stopband 名称更贴合阻带抑制意图

scoring.metric_rationale: 这两个指标直接对应用户的两个核心且 competing 的需求：1530-1565 nm 波段高透射用于接收量子信号，400-700 nm 波段高反射用于抑制太阳背景杂散光。仅用两个指标覆盖请求，避免额外指标稀释核心需求的权重。未将层数限制纳入指标是因为这是制造约束而非光学性能指标，由单独机制处理。未指定角度和偏振是因为用户未明确要求，使用默认通道。
scoring.formula_rationale: The user assigns equal priority to both objectives using identical phrasing ('尽可能完整地接收' and '尽可能反射'), indicating neither signal transmission nor background rejection should dominate the ranking. Since both metrics are normalized fractions between 0 and 1, adding them directly treats each requirement as equally important without introducing arbitrary coefficients. This ensures that maximizing the score requires high performance in both the telecom passband and the visible stopband simultaneously.

routes.title: Periodic quarter-wave Bragg stack centered at 550 nm for visible reflection
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave stack with 15 HfO2/SiO2 pairs centered at 550 nm will achieve high reflectance across 400-700 nm while maintaining high transmittance at 1530-1565 nm, with performance improving as layer thicknesses are tuned from the ideal quarter-wave condition.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflectors create a photonic stopband centered at the design wavelength. By centering the stopband at 550 nm (middle of 400-700 nm), the 1530-1565 nm band falls well outside the stopband and should transmit. The HfO2/SiO2 index contrast provides sufficient reflectivity per interface.
routes.topology: Air | (hfo2, sio2) repeated 15 times | sio2 substrate, total 30 layers
known_risks: Fixed period may not cover full 400-700 nm band evenly
Edge wavelengths (400 nm, 700 nm) may have lower reflectance
30 layers may accumulate stress or absorption losses

routes.title: Chirped thickness stack to broaden visible reflection band
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A chirped multilayer stack with systematically varying layer thicknesses will achieve more uniform reflectance across 400-700 nm than a periodic stack, at the cost of slightly reduced peak reflectance, while maintaining transmission at 1530-1565 nm.
routes.design_principle: Chirped Bragg reflectors vary the optical thickness of layers across the stack, creating multiple overlapping stopbands that merge into a broader reflection band. By grading thickness from values appropriate for 400 nm at one end to 700 nm at the other, the full visible band can be covered.

routes.title: Defect-cavity stack with transmission resonance at 1550 nm
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Introducing a half-wave defect cavity layer within a Bragg stack will create a narrow transmission resonance at 1550 nm center wavelength, achieving higher peak transmittance in 1530-1565 nm than a simple periodic stack, while maintaining visible reflection.
routes.design_principle: Defect modes in photonic crystals create localized states within the stopband. By placing a half-wave cavity (optical thickness = λ/2 at 1550 nm) within a Bragg reflector, a transmission peak appears at the cavity wavelength while the surrounding layers maintain visible reflection.

routes.title: Quarter-wave dichroic longpass stack tuned for visible rejection and telecom transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 30-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack centered at 550 nm will produce a high-reflection stopband covering 400-700 nm while transmitting 1530-1565 nm, and individual layer thickness tuning can improve the balance between the two bands without exceeding the 30-layer constraint.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create high reflectance when optical thickness (n×d) equals λ/4 at the design wavelength. The reflection bandwidth scales with the index contrast ratio (nH/nL). Wavelengths significantly longer than the quarter-wave center see reduced optical thickness and transmit. Starting with high-index at the air interface maximizes front-surface reflection contribution.
